title: Warn when Elementor editor compatibility fallback runs
description: Show an editor-only warning when the Filter Controller depends on compatibility fallback behavior to synchronize Elementor widget controls.
objective: Make Elementor editor fallback usage visible instead of silent, so future Elementor updates can be diagnosed without guessing whether native panel refresh failed.
inputs_required: Guilherme concern that the Elementor integration could become fragile after Elementor updates
Existing editor fallback paths for settings command failure and Style panel DOM cadence
expected_outputs: The editor records compatibility fallback reasons once per session.
A visible warning appears in the Elementor panel when fallback behavior has been applied.
The browser console receives a warning with the fallback reason.
The warning copy clarifies that frontend output still comes from widget settings.
Plugin asset version is bumped for cache busting.
acceptance_criteria: When the Style panel DOM cadence fallback touches controls, the Elementor panel shows a compatibility fallback warning.
When the Elementor settings command throws, the same warning path is used.
Repeated sync loops do not spam duplicate warnings for the same reason.
The warning is editor-only and does not alter frontend rendering or saved preset data.
verification: JS syntax check passes for the editor asset.
PHP syntax check passes for touched PHP files.
git diff --check passes in root and plugin.

budgets.complexity_budget: moderate and bounded to editor assets
budgets.context_budget: Elementor editor sync helpers, editor CSS, localized strings, and plugin version
budgets.research_budget: local plugin code and existing Elementor fallback paths
budgets.validation_budget: syntax, lint, composer, static diff checks, and Guilherme visual QA

risks: The warning insertion itself uses Elementor panel DOM anchors, so it is also best-effort.
The warning may appear whenever the current implementation uses DOM cadence, even if the widget output is healthy.
Nuanced placement and motion in the Elementor editor still require Guilherme visual QA.
